what: First attempt at a quality baseline for Strata SQ-15, and why it is void

result.accuracy: 100% on 40 tasks at both temperature 1.0 and 0.0

why_void: The public Benchmark 500 manifest carries prompt HASHES, not prompt text, so I wrote probe prompts from templates instead of using the real items.
Those templates produce ONE question per suite, repeated 10 times. The run is therefore 4 distinct questions asked 10 times each, not 40 tasks.
The 4 questions are trivial: 17*3+2, a textbook free-fall question, a textbook intensive-property question, and a one-clause sentence rewrite.
100% on 4 easy questions at two temperatures says the model is not broken. It says nothing about accuracy on the 500-task suite.
what_a_real_quality_baseline_needs: the actual prompt text for each task, which lives in the dataset rows the manifest points at (dataset + dataset_revision + source_id), not in the manifest itself
a fetch of each dataset at the pinned revision, then the row matching source_id
the official scorer per suite, since IFEval and BFCL have format-sensitive graders and a regex substitute will not match published numbers
enough tasks for a confidence interval: 40 tasks gives +/-15 points at 95% on a 50% accuracy, which cannot distinguish 96.68% from 100%
honest_position: There is still no quality number for Strata. The 100% figure is discarded, not reported. Speed (22.6 tok/s) remains the only measured Strata figure we have.
cost_estimate_for_the_real_run: Fetching 4 suites at pinned revisions is roughly 1-3 GB of data and the official scorer work is a day. Sampling 100-200 real tasks per suite at ~20 tok/s is several hours of GPU per suite.
